name: IL-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about five points on the partisan baseline
Budzinski holds a massive financial edge: $2.6M cash on hand versus Wilson's $12K
Prediction markets price her near 94% to win
First-term incumbency adds a modest advantage
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Budzinski: a D+5 district, a favorable national environment for Democrats, incumbency, and an overwhelming fundraising advantage over Wilson, whose campaign has almost no cash. Markets agree, pricing her around 94%, so the forecast stays in Safe D territory with a slightly trimmed margin given the absence of polling.
model.watch: A late outside-spending surge for Wilson or a sharply worse national environment for Democrats could pull this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term Democrat Nikki Budzinski seeks re-election in an Illinois district that leans Democratic by about five points. She enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised nearly $2.9 million and holding $2.6 million on hand, while Republican Jeff Wilson has raised under $350,000 and reports only about $12,000 in the bank. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race so far.

No public general-election polling is available, and no expert raters have flagged the contest as competitive. Prediction markets give Budzinski roughly a 94% chance of winning. With the fundamentals, money, and markets all aligned, the seat is rated Safe Democratic, with a modest haircut to the expected margin to account for the lack of direct polling.
